summary: 14-day glycemic analysis demonstrates outstanding control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and low variability (CV 12.9%). Basal rates maintain overnight stability, and meal bolus settings (CR 9-12 g/U) manage post-prandial excursions effectively with full recovery to baseline within 4 hours. AAPS SMB and UAM automation operate safely within established IOB and max basal boundaries without compensating for profile defects.
issues: Transient post-prandial glucose peak reaching 188 mg/dL during Weekend Brunch (10:30) following larger, higher-fat carbohydrate intake (68g carbs).
strengths: Exceptional Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time Below 70 mg/dL.
Very low glucose variability with Coefficient of Variation (CV) at 12.9% and Standard Deviation of 15.1 mg/dL.
Overnight glucose remains flat and stable between 102 and 113 mg/dL across all 14 days without fasting drift.
AAPS automation (SMB/UAM) successfully handles residual post-meal absorption without causing insulin stacking or hypoglycemia.
safety_notes: This analysis is for decision-support and educational review only; always independently verify data and consult your healthcare team before adjusting insulin settings.
Never modify multiple dependent settings (e.g., basal, CR, and ISF) simultaneously.
Make parameter changes conservatively, testing one change at a time and monitoring CGM readings closely.
education: Time in Range above 70% with CV below 36% represents international clinical targets for type 1 diabetes management.
E-carbs (extended carbs in AAPS) modify the internal carbohydrate absorption model and do not trigger a pump extended bolus.
Prebolus timing helps synchronize insulin peak action with carbohydrate absorption to reduce post-prandial glucose peaks.

recommendations.title: Refine Weekend Brunch Prebolus and Meal Strategy
recommendations.description: For larger, higher-fat weekend meals (e.g., 68g brunch), glucose peaks at 188 mg/dL at 2 hours before returning to baseline by 4 hours. Extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15-20 minutes or utilizing a split bolus / e-carbs (e.g. 60% immediate, 20g e-carbs over 120 min) can help suppress the 2-hour peak while letting AAPS automation handle late fat/protein impact.
